mappings.summary: LangGraph owns graph/task/checkpoint execution identities, but the inspected public surface does not define a canonical logical identity for an external consequential effect across replay attempts.

evidence.claim: Task and checkpoint payloads expose runtime-owned task/checkpoint identifiers.
Crash recovery discussion shows external side-effect identity can remain outside checkpoint identity.

mappings.caveat: Runtime task identity and logical external-effect identity solve different scopes.

mappings.summary: LangGraph durability defines persistence timing for graph state, while the public Durability contract does not itself define authoritative external-effect evidence.

evidence.claim: Durability is documented as sync/async/exit persistence timing.
The issue distinguishes checkpoint/write recovery from whether an external effect already happened.

mappings.caveat: This is not a LangGraph defect claim; external-effect confirmation may intentionally belong to application/tool integrations.

mappings.summary: The inspected LangGraph public runtime statuses do not expose a first-class UNKNOWN external-effect outcome that blocks blind replay until reconciliation.

evidence.claim: RunStatus covers pending/running/error/success/timeout/interrupted; it is run lifecycle, not an external-effect uncertainty state.
Crash-after-effect scenarios can leave the application unable to infer whether the external effect committed.

mappings.caveat: A graph run being interrupted or errored is not equivalent to an external effect being unresolved.

mappings.summary: LangGraph has retry, replay, task identity, and checkpoint durability mechanisms, but they do not by themselves preserve one application-level logical external effect across all replay attempts.

evidence.claim: RetryPolicy and Durability are first-class runtime concepts.
The recovery discussion includes duplicate/re-executed side-effect pressure after crash.

mappings.caveat: AEA-007 is specifically about effect-intent multiplicity; LangGraph retry semantics are broader graph execution mechanics.

mappings.summary: LangGraph does not prescribe a cross-domain authoritative readback source that must close an ambiguous external effect before the next dependent decision.

evidence.claim: Discussion identifies the external-effect gap after durable recovery but leaves downstream reconciliation to application/runtime integration.

mappings.caveat: This may be intentionally out of scope for a general graph runtime.

mappings.summary: LangGraph checkpoint/task correlation does not attempt to define AEE v0.2's trusted evidence binding between logical effect id, attempt id, and evidence identity.

evidence.claim: Checkpoint/task payloads describe graph runtime state rather than a trusted external-effect evidence registry.

mappings.caveat: Orthogonal means different responsibility, not missing functionality.

mappings.summary: The inspected LangGraph durability surface does not define verifier identity or attested/verified trust levels for external-effect evidence.

evidence.claim: Durability and checkpoint payload types do not define external evidence verifier/trust semantics.

mappings.caveat: Such provenance may belong to an application-specific integration layer.

mappings.summary: LangGraph can preserve graph execution state across recovery, but the inspected public contract does not fail closed on missing external-effect provenance because that provenance is not part of its model.

evidence.claim: The failure case demonstrates a recovery gap between graph durability and knowledge of an external effect.

mappings.caveat: This mapping compares guarantees, not product scope; LangGraph may reasonably delegate effect reconciliation to users.

declaration.limitations: This is an analyst-authored comparison against LangGraph public code and issue discussion at one revision. It is not a LangGraph compatibility result and does not assert that application-level integrations cannot implement stronger effect guarantees.
